content.summary: Welcome to the reading mission for unit A2.2-M04. In this lesson, you will read short movie reviews and learn how to express your own opinions about films, genres, and plots using everyday English.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Opinion phrases such as 'In my opinion...', 'I think that...', and evaluative adjectives.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Film genres, plot descriptions, and critical vocabulary like thrilling, predictable, and brilliant.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning movie reviews for specific details and skimming paragraphs to identify the main opinion of the writer.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short movie reviews and film summaries.
Locate specific details such as film genres, plot points, and personal recommendations.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns for giving critical opinions.

contextWarmup.prompt: How often do you go to the cinema or watch movies at home with your friends?
options: I watch movies almost every weekend with my family.
I never watch movies or television shows.
I only watch educational videos on my phone.
contextWarmup.explanation: Watching movies on weekends is a very common social hobby and leisure activity for A2 learners.

rules: Use opinion opening phrases like 'In my opinion, ...', 'I think that ...', 'I found it + adjective', or 'For me, the movie was + adjective'.
Use evaluative adjectives to describe films: thrilling, boring, predictable, brilliant, disappointing, and entertaining.
To recommend a film to others, use: 'I recommend + film title', 'You should watch ...', or 'It is worth watching if you like ...'.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Confusing opinion phrases and simple descriptions
commonTrap.explanation: Learners often write just 'The movie is good' without explaining why or using specific evaluative adjectives.
commonTrap.wrong: The film is nice and I like it.
commonTrap.correct: In my opinion, the film is brilliant because the acting is excellent and the plot is thrilling.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Movie Reviews and Critical Opinions

content.summary: Learn how to write clear movie reviews by expressing personal opinions, using evaluative adjectives, and giving film recommendations in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Stating Personal Opinions
blueprintItems.formula: In my opinion / I think (that) + subject + verb + adjective
blueprintItems.example: In my opinion, the new action movie is thrilling.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Describing Plot and Acting
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + was/were + evaluative adjective (plus contrast with 'but')
blueprintItems.example: The plot was predictable, but the acting was brilliant.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Recommending Films to Others
blueprintItems.formula: I recommend + film title + because + reason
blueprintItems.example: I recommend this comedy because it is very entertaining.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize movie titles and proper names.
mechanicsRules.why: Titles of films and proper names require capital letters in English.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma after introductory opinion phrases.
mechanicsRules.badExample: In my opinion the film was boring.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: In my opinion, the film was boring.
mechanicsRules.why: Introductory phrases like 'In my opinion' need a comma before the main clause.

mechanicsRules.rule: Match singular and plural forms with 'is' and 'are' or 'was' and 'were'.
mechanicsRules.why: Plural nouns like 'actors' require the plural verb 'were'.

sections.title: Pronunciation & Delivery Guide for Cinema Discussions

content.summary: This guide helps you discuss film genres, describe plots, and express critical opinions clearly. You will learn how to stress evaluative adjectives and use natural intonation when sharing your views.
content.audioGuidance: Focus on clear vowel sounds in adjectives such as thrilling, predictable, and brilliant. Keep your rhythm steady and stress the most important words in your sentences.

pillars.name: Adjective Stress
pillars.target: Correct syllable emphasis on evaluation words
pillars.explanation: When expressing opinions, emphasize the main syllable in words like disappointing or entertaining to sound clear and confident.

pillars.name: Sentence Rhythm
pillars.target: Linking words smoothly in movie discussions
pillars.explanation: Connect auxiliary verbs and pronouns naturally so your speech flows without awkward pauses.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the primary stress stays on the first syllable in both forms.
The stress remains on the second syllable for both the adjective and noun forms.
The stress shifts from the third syllable in the adjective to the first syllable in the verb base.
Both forms maintain primary stress on the third syllable.
